subject: Australia recruitment matching / recruitment services
reason: Multiple distinct AusTender award-first clusters independently show recruitment/personnel-recruitment demand across many buyers and suppliers. This appears economically distinct from contractor bodyshopping: the paid output may be search/matching/placement itself, which is potentially highly automatable and asset-light. Must decompose executive search, permanent recruitment, temp staffing, RPO, screening and contractor placement before final business judgment.
next_test: Deep title/buyer/winner decomposition and buyer recurrence.

subject: Australia training / education-and-training services
reason: Very large and fragmented historical surface, but current cluster labels mix tuition, instructor-led training, education purchases, workshops and potentially digital/e-learning content. SPM asymmetry varies radically by subtype.
next_test: Decompose by delivery model: digital content/e-learning, training design, instructor-led, certification/tuition, training materials, assessment.

subject: Australia specialist assurance review / evaluation services
reason: Large repeated Department of Finance cluster with many suppliers suggests a review/evaluation micro-market. Potentially lean if work is document/evidence review; may instead require accredited senior specialists. Needs semantic and winner-archetype decomposition.
next_test: Sample titles/winners and determine credential requirements and repeatable review outputs.

subject: Local service subcontractor aggregation — US janitorial/custodial/pest/laundry/grounds
reason: Historical award-first cohorts show broad buyers and suppliers. SPM could theoretically win/coordinate work and subcontract local operators, with automation in sourcing, quoting, scheduling and reporting. Physical QA, locality, set-asides, insurance and margin leakage are serious unknowns.
next_test: Analyze supplier archetypes, award sizes, buyer recurrence, geography and likely set-aside/local execution burden.

subject: Expert witness / litigative consultant network
reason: US archive shows thousands of expert-witness/litigative-consultant awards and hundreds of suppliers. Could support an expert-network/intermediary model, but many awards may contract directly with individual experts or regulated professionals. Intermediary economics are unproven.
next_test: Identify winner archetypes: individual experts vs firms vs expert-network intermediaries; measure repeat buyers and concentration.

subject: Interpretation / interpreter services as distinct language-service lane
reason: Separate historical US clusters explicitly procure interpreter/interpretation services across many buyers and suppliers. It is distinct from written translation. Live/human delivery reduces AI compression, but remote interpreter-network aggregation may remain asset-light.
next_test: Decompose remote/video/phone vs onsite interpretation and agency vs individual supplier patterns.

subject: Australia event management / venue-hire aggregation
reason: Event-management cohorts are highly supplier-fragmented, but venue hire is a different economic model and physical coordination may dominate. Keep separate and test event-management-only economics.
next_test: Separate event-management agencies from venue-only awards, production, AV, catering and travel components.

subject: Commodity distribution from DLA-style food/water clusters
reason: Large record counts are concentrated in very few buyers and low-ticket repetitive commodity orders. Historical volume alone does not imply an attractive SPM asymmetry; logistics, approved suppliers and thin margins likely dominate.
next_test: Only revisit if a buyer-agnostic, high-margin or unusual commodity niche emerges.

subject: Medical laboratory testing aggregation
reason: The discovered testing clusters are physical/medical laboratory services, not generic remote QA/testing. Regulation and physical execution dominate SPM's native edge.
next_test: No priority expansion unless non-medical remote testing categories emerge separately.

subject: Rental/leasing mechanism tag containing US court reporter services
reason: Court reporter services are not evidence of rental/leasing merely because a broad mechanism regex matched the cluster. Reject the mechanism assignment only; keep court-reporting records for language/legal/document-service analysis.
next_test: Fix mechanism regex and consider court reporting as its own document/legal support lane.
